name: Mossy boulder
description: A rounded, weathered cool-grey boulder with thick clumped moss cushions in three greens on its upward-facing top and ledges, a little moss creeping down the shoulders and bare stone on the sides and base. Variants are a boulder with a smaller stone leaning against it, a small single stone and a large heap of three stacked, merged boulders.

provenance.prompt: A rounded weathered grey boulder with moss on its top faces: soft rounded stone (cool grey, about (0.3, 0.3, 0.28) linear, darker in the cracks), thick moss cushions only on the upward-facing top surfaces and ledges, a little moss creeping down the shoulders, bare stone on the sides and the base sitting on the ground. Three variants: rock_mossy (about 0.7 m across, 0.5 m high, one boulder with a crack or a second smaller stone leaning against it), rock_mossy_small (about 0.35 m across, 0.25 m high) and rock_mossy_large (about 1.2 m across, 0.8 m high, two or three stacked and merged boulders). Moss uses the clumped painted-look idea: small lumpy cushions in three greens, darker in the hollows, lit on top. Category decor. Under 4,000 triangles per variant. Painted look (match a painted isometric forest road): foliage is clumped leaf cards with value variation, never single flat planes and never one smooth blob. Build each clump from many small leaf cards (thin bevel-free boxes about 4 mm thick, or strongly squashed subdiv=1 blobs) tilted at seeded angles around a darker core, in three greens: a deep shadow green inside and underneath, a mid olive green, and a lit yellow-green on the top and outer rims, so it reads dark inside, lit at the rims. Earthy, slightly desaturated palette like grass_tuft and pebbles (olive about (0.1, 0.13, 0.035) linear). Low triangle count, decor scale.
